title: Avatar Blend Shape | Clo 2026.0 Features Deep Dive
description:
The new gluing feature in CLO 2026.0 allows you to import avatars with blend shapes to freely customize various body shapes and detailed facial expressions.
Check out other new features here:https://clo3d.com/en/clo/features  

Questions? Comment below or ask in our CLO discord server: https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/7814962429977-How-can-I-join-CLO-Discord?utm_campaign=multi_item_banner_JointheOfficialCLODiscord&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=later-linkinbio

transcript: Hey everyone, it's Phoebe here, and I'm going to walk you through this really cool new feature we have for our avatars for blending. So let's dive on in and have some fun while we learn. So here I have my cloud window open and all set. What I just want us to know is this is good for external avatars, like avatars that have been created in other softwares, and especially other 3D softwares, where you have those different, like, deformation or different shaping all applied to the avatar. So something like this, if you've created multiple shapings for one avatar, will now be able to read both a body and even, like, a facial expression like these. Really cool, right? So all of that you'll be able to see. Now, again, this is not for CLO avatars. This is for... EXTERNAL avatars that were created. To get to it, it's pretty easy. You're going to first, like, simulate, of course, and have, like, just quickly. Then, now that I've simulated, I'm going to go into my avatar editor. Then in the avatar editor, I'll go all the way over to blend shape, as you can see here. Now, I have the body here, so I know that my body has a blended shape. Just using this slider here. I can make it so that the shape is changing. Super simple and easy. I can then use some of those bitmaps to see how it's working because I've simulated and it's simulating right now. So that pressure map works. I can turn off simulation, obviously. But it's this slider here that will allow me to control how I want to see the blended body shapes. Let's do a little bit more fun something with, like, facial expressions. So I'm going to bring in another avatar that has a lot of blended facial expressions. That was created in another software. Now that I have this avatar, you see there's a ton of options here and I can scroll down. There's all these face options and it's separated out into, like, body, face, all of that. What's really helpful is something like this. So I can, like, adjust. Of course, with my sliders and I'm seeing my face change a little bit. What's nice is these stars off to the left. If I select them, I'm favoriting them. And then if I just want to show my favorites, I just go to that star at the very top to just see the favorites that I have. But again, the act is pretty simple. It's just using that slider to get to the expression that I want. Really nice, right? Thanks so much for watching. If you have any questions, please feel free to leave a comment. If you have any questions, use that comment section down below. Don't forget to like and subscribe and check out all of the great videos we have for you. And keep having fun in Clow. Thanks so much.
markdown_content: ## Overview: Blend Shape Support for External Avatars (Non-CLO) This section explains the new blend shape feature and clarifies that it targets **external avatars** (created in other software), not **CLO avatars**. It also describes what kinds of deformation and facial expression data can be read. The feature is designed for **external avatars**—for example, avatars created in other **3D software**—where multiple deformation or shaping setups have been applied to the character. With this capability, the system can read both **body blend shapes** and **facial expression blend shapes** from those externally created assets. It’s important to note: **this is not for CLO avatars**. The workflow is intended for avatars authored elsewhere, with blend shape data imported into CLO 2026.0 for visualization and editing. --- ## Where to Find It: Simulation → Avatar Editor → Blend Shape This section covers the navigation path to access the blend shape controls inside the **Avatar Editor**, including how simulation relates to previewing results. To use the feature: 1. Open the **cloud** environment (the presenter mentions having the cloud window open). 2. **Simulate** first. 3. After simulation, go to the **Avatar Editor**. 4. In the Avatar Editor, navigate to **Blend Shape** (shown as a dedicated area/section). Once in **Blend Shape**, the presenter demonstrates that the avatar’s body has blend shape data available, including a **slider** for controlling the blend amount and previewing how the shape changes. --- ## Body Blend Shapes: Slider Control and Pressure Map Preview This section describes how to manipulate **body blend shapes** using the blend slider and how to use the provided visualization tools (including a pressure map) during simulation. In the **Blend Shape** section, the **body** blend shapes can be controlled using a **slider**. Moving the slider changes the avatar’s body shape, allowing you to preview the blended result. The presenter also notes the use of **bitmaps** to understand how the blend behaves. Since the avatar is currently **simulating**, the **pressure map** works as part of the preview. You can also **turn off simulation** when desired, while still using the blend shape slider to control which blended body shape you want to view. --- ## Facial Expression Blend Shapes: Browsing, Sliders, and Favorites This section explains how to work with imported **facial expression** blend shapes, including how the UI organizes options and how to favorite frequently used expressions. To try facial expressions, the presenter imports another avatar that includes **many blended facial expressions** created in another software. After importing: - There are **many options** available. - The options are organized into categories such as **body** and **face** (the UI is separated by type). For facial expressions, you can: - Scroll through the facial options. - Use **sliders** to adjust the expression and see the face change in real time. A helpful UI feature is **faster selection via favorites**: - Expression entries have **stars** on the left. - Selecting a star **favorites** that expression. - A star control at the **top** lets you show only your **favorite** expressions, making it easier to quickly access preferred facial shapes. ---
